lesson.title: 14.1.5 Weather and Access Windows: Calendars and Optional Work

blueprint.contract: Also reads each circuit's windows (none: the whole season) and must flag (none: optional), and the season's crew_off, crew id to spans of weeks off (none: every crew works every week). Circuit gains `windows` and `must`, after `growth`; Season gains `crew_off: dict[str, Weeks]` between `months` and `circuits`, so a Season is built as Season(name, budget, crews, months, crew_off, circuits). Weeks is tuple[tuple[int, int], ...], a module-level alias in data.py.
blueprint.idea: A missing calendar column means no calendar, so older exports still load.

lesson.title: 14.1.5 Weather and Access Windows: Calendars and Optional Work

blueprint.signature: def scenario(size: str = "small", seed: int = 54) -> dict
blueprint.contract: Also, from its own stream named 'access', one circuit at a time in order: must when a draw of random() is below 0.15; then a River circuit has the window [8, last week], a Hills circuit has the windows [0, 5] and [14, last week] when a second draw is below 0.5, and every other circuit no windows. The season's crew_off gives K1 the weeks [10, 11] and, with more than one crew, the last crew (K2 in the small season, K6 in the medium) the weeks [14, 17]. The season's dict holds `crew_off` between `months` and `circuits`.
blueprint.idea: A column drawn from its own stream leaves the values of every earlier column as they were.

lesson.title: 14.1.5 Weather and Access Windows: Calendars and Optional Work

blueprint.signature: def start_domain(c: Circuit, h: int) -> cp_model.Domain
blueprint.contract: Returns every first week that keeps a trim of the circuit's weeks inside one of its windows (the whole season when it has none) and inside the season: one interval per window long enough, and an empty domain when none is.
blueprint.idea: An access window is a domain on the start, one interval per window, so a trim never runs across a closed week.

lesson.title: 4.5.2 Cumulative Resources: Crews and Outage Windows

blueprint.contract: As before, with each start taking its values from start_domain, no crew options for a circuit whose domain is empty, each crew's weeks off as fixed intervals in that crew's no-overlap, and every must circuit trimmed.
blueprint.idea: A crew's weeks off are fixed intervals its trims may not overlap.

blueprint.contract: As before, keeping every calendar; when the must circuits cannot all be trimmed, a Plan with the status INFEASIBLE and no trims. (The reference also takes an `overrides` argument that it ignores, typed with a stub Override dataclass in data.py, ready for the next lesson; this step's tests do not use it.)
blueprint.idea: A must is a hard rule, so a season that cannot keep it has no plan.
